source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 7–8. All 115 exact original records are hashed, including source annotations at 7:4, 7:32, 7:40, 7:55, 7:59 and 7:68. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Render raising the lamps as lighting with setting up noted as an alternative; keep seven and direction without inventing a particular geometry.
Preserve the whole-work span and repeated hammered description; use passive for the unnamed maker rather than assigning fabrication to Moses.
Distinguish Moses sprinkling from the Levites shaving and washing; retain all flesh scope and avoid inventing the water’s ingredients.
Preserve the switch from they to you, both bulls, the grain contents and the second bull’s sin-offering designation.
Keep the people as hand-laying agents and the Levites as recipients; do not assert an unstated representative procedure.
Preserve wave offering applied to people and its source/purpose; present avoids asserting a physical lifting procedure the passage does not explain.
Keep the second hand-laying stage, distinct actors, two offering assignments and atonement for the Levites; retain command to Moses rather than silently replacing him with Aaron.
Retain the addressed Moses’ presentation and priestly recipients as written; do not collapse into the Aaron instruction in verse 11.
Preserve after this and the repeated purification/presentation instruction without fabricating a second ceremony.
Render the doubled given as wholly; retain replacement, male firstborn scope and the womb image rather than reducing it to eldest regardless of maternal birth order.
Keep both human and animal firstborn and divine agency in Egypt’s deaths; retain sanctification to God without softening the harm.

Divide the long clause while retaining all five mentions of Israelites, divine gift, priestly recipients, service, atonement and the plague-prevention purpose; do not recast Levites as sacrificing priests.
Distinguish self-purification from Aaron’s presentation and atonement, preserving his repeated name and purification as purpose.
Preserve twenty-five instead of harmonizing chapter 4’s thirty; express the service-company idiom while retaining male eligibility.
Keep mandatory withdrawal at fifty and cessation of the specified service, preparing for the narrower continuing role in verse 26.
Preserve assistance and keeping charge alongside the prohibition on work; do not claim total exclusion or invent a precise light-work/heavy-work division.
